subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` remain a supported break-glass Gateway mode, or should OpenClaw remove or harden it with additional CSRF/fetch-metadata controls?
rationale: The current code and docs intentionally expose this dangerous operator-selected fallback, but changing it can alter existing non-loopback deployments and the security boundary cannot be chosen safely by automation.

options.title: Accept documented dangerous mode
options.body: Treat the current flag as an explicit out-of-scope break-glass tradeoff unless a concrete bypass beyond operator-enabled dangerous config is shown.

options.title: Harden while preserving the flag
options.body: Keep the config surface but require an additional browser CSRF or `Sec-Fetch-*` gate and add focused Gateway origin tests and docs.

options.title: Remove the fallback
options.body: Delete the flag and add any needed doctor/docs guidance for users who relied on Host-header origin policy.

recommendation.title: Accept documented dangerous mode
recommendation.body: Treat the current flag as an explicit out-of-scope break-glass tradeoff unless a concrete bypass beyond operator-enabled dangerous config is shown.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the origin-check path and the explicit non-loopback origin fallback policy, making him the best available routing owner for the security-boundary choice.
